problems.prompt: At the cathode of this copper electrorefining cell, the half-reaction is:
problems.explain: Reduction happens at the cathode: Cu²⁺ ions gain two electrons and deposit as solid copper.

problems.prompt: Why is the anode in this cell made of copper metal rather than an inert material?
choices: So it dissolves (Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻), replenishing Cu²⁺ and keeping the bath concentration roughly constant
Because inert anodes are more expensive
So the anode gains mass instead of the cathode
It has no effect on the reaction — any conductor works identically
problems.explain: A copper anode oxidizes and dissolves at the same rate copper deposits on the cathode, transferring copper from anode to cathode without depleting the solution — the basis of electrorefining/electroplating.

problems.prompt: According to Faraday's law, the mass of copper deposited is directly proportional to ____ passed through the cell.
problems.explain: m = ItM/(zF): mass is proportional to charge Q = It, for fixed z, F, M.

problems.prompt: If I = 1.0 A flows for t = 965 s (z = 2, F = 96485 C/mol, M = 63.55 g/mol), what mass of copper (in grams) deposits at the cathode?
